skins.title: End-of-day backup
skins.situation: At the end of each day, you and Farah each decide whether to save your work to the team’s shared drive or keep it only on your laptop.

incentives.m3.s.both: Saving to the shared drive protects your own work, and you also gain when Farah’s work is there. The same holds for Farah.

skins.timing: You both decide at the end of the day, separately.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know what Farah will do today.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your saving and Farah’s saving

skins.title: Before the group ride
skins.situation: Before a group cycling ride, you and Vikram each decide whether to check your own tyres or skip it.

incentives.m3.s.both: Checking your tyres makes your own ride safer, and the ride goes better for you when Vikram has checked his. The same holds for Vikram.

skins.timing: You both get ready at home, at the same time.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know whether Vikram will check.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your check and Vikram’s check

skins.title: The shared fridge
skins.situation: You and your flatmate Yash each decide whether to label your food in the shared fridge this week.

incentives.m3.s.both: Labelling your own food keeps it from being eaten by mistake, and the fridge is easier for you when Yash labels his too. The same holds for Yash.

skins.timing: You both shop and stock the fridge separately this week.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know whether Yash will label.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your labelling and Yash’s labelling

skins.title: The broken street light
skins.situation: A street light on your lane is broken. You and your neighbour Anjali each decide whether to report it on the ward office’s app.

incentives.m3.s.both: Each report moves the repair up the list, and only people who report get updates on it. The same holds for Anjali.

skins.timing: You both decide this evening, separately.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know whether Anjali will report.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your report and Anjali’s report

skins.title: Fresh bread
skins.situation: You run a bakery, and Mr Paul runs the café across the road and buys your bread. Tonight you decide whether to bake early or late, and Mr Paul decides whether to collect in the morning or the afternoon.

incentives.m3.s.one: Baking early lets you finish before the shop opens, which matters most to you; you also gain when Mr Paul collects in the morning. Mr Paul wants fresh bread: morning pickup if you bake early, afternoon if you bake late.

skins.timing: You both decide tonight, separately.
skins.information: You both know what the other wants. You don’t know when Mr Paul will collect.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your baking and Mr Paul’s pickup

skins.title: The vegetable cart
skins.situation: Raju sells vegetables from a cart, either at the market square or by the park, and decides this evening where to stand. You buy from him and decide where to walk for your vegetables.

incentives.m3.s.one@B: You only get your vegetables if you go where the cart is, and the square is nearer your home. The square gets Raju far more passing trade, and he also likes regulars like you to come to the square.

skins.timing: You both decide this evening, separately. Raju’s phone is switched off.
skins.information: You know how Raju’s trade works. You don’t know where he will stand.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for Raju’s spot and yours

skins.title: Meeting for a picnic
skins.situation: You are meeting your friend Sunil for a picnic. You decide whether to come by bus or by car, and Sunil decides whether to wait for you at the bus stop or at the car park.

incentives.m3.s.one: The bus is cheaper and quicker for you than driving, and you would rather Sunil waits at the bus stop. Sunil wants to wait where you will arrive.

skins.timing: You both set off at the same time. Neither can reach the other.
skins.information: You both know what the other wants. You don’t know where Sunil will wait.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your travel and Sunil’s waiting spot

skins.title: Meeting for a picnic
skins.situation: You are meeting your friend Sunil for a picnic. Sunil decides whether to come by bus or by car, and you decide whether to wait for him at the bus stop or at the car park.

incentives.m3.s.one@B: You want to wait where Sunil will arrive. The bus is cheaper and quicker for him than driving, and he would rather you wait at the bus stop.

skins.timing: You both set off at the same time. Neither can reach the other.
skins.information: You both know what the other wants. You don’t know how Sunil will travel.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for Sunil’s travel and your waiting spot
skins.mirrorPurpose: Seat rotation with a learner-role purpose: in sk.m3.picnic.a the learner holds the sure choice; here the learner must predict the other person from their incentives and then respond (m3.l2 seat-B items).

skins.title: Rows and columns
skins.situation: At the same moment, you pick a row, top, middle or bottom, and the other side picks a column, left, centre or right.

incentives.m3.s.elim: Each of you wants a high number for yourself. Your best cell is bottom-right; the other side’s best is middle-centre or bottom-left.

skins.timing: You both pick at the same moment.
skins.information: Each side sees the whole table. You don’t know the other side’s column.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your row and the other side’s column

skins.title: Side-by-side stalls
skins.situation: You and Leena run food stalls side by side at a weekend market. You choose your main dish: rolls, thalis or snacks. At the same time Leena chooses her drink: juice, lassi or tea.

incentives.m3.s.elim: What you each earn depends on how the two menus fit together. You earn most selling snacks next to tea; Leena earns most with lassi next to thalis, or juice next to snacks.

skins.timing: You both fix your menus on Friday, separately.
skins.information: You both know the market well. You don’t know what Leena will choose.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your dish and Leena’s drink

skins.title: Two shift patterns
skins.situation: You and Pranav plan next week’s shifts for your two teams. You choose a pattern for yours: early, standard or late. At the same moment Pranav chooses his: split, full or short.

incentives.m3.s.elim: How each week goes depends on how the two patterns fit. Your best week is late against short; Pranav’s best is full against standard, or split against late.

skins.timing: You both send your pattern at the same moment.
skins.information: You both know how the teams work. You don’t know Pranav’s pattern.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your pattern and Pranav’s pattern

skins.title: The hockey plan
skins.situation: In a hockey match you choose your team’s plan: press, hold or counter. At the same moment the other coach, Ms Gill, chooses hers: wide, central or deep.

incentives.m3.s.elim: How the match goes for each side depends on how the plans meet. Your best result is counter against deep; Ms Gill’s best is central against hold, or wide against counter.

skins.timing: Both coaches set their plans before the match, at the same time.
skins.information: You both know each other’s teams. You don’t know Ms Gill’s plan.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your plan and Ms Gill’s plan

skins.title: The price-match scheme
skins.situation: You run a stationery shop in a mall, opposite Mr Khanna’s. This week the mall offers a free price-match scheme: members may match any rival sale price. You decide whether to join, and Mr Khanna decides whether to run a sale.

incentives.m3.s.weak: Joining is free and changes nothing on a normal week. If Mr Khanna runs a sale, matching it keeps some customers; outside the scheme you lose them. His sale pays him when you stay out, and costs him when you join.

skins.timing: You both decide on Monday, separately. The mall names its members only at the end of the week.
skins.information: You both know how the scheme works. You don’t know whether Mr Khanna will run a sale.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your choice and Mr Khanna’s

skins.title: Shapes and arrows
skins.situation: At the same moment, you choose a square or a circle, and the other side chooses up or down.

incentives.m3.s.weak: With up, square and circle give you the same; with down, square gives you more. The other side wants up with your square and down with your circle.

skins.timing: You both choose at the same moment.
skins.information: Each side sees the whole table. You don’t know the other side’s choice.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your shape and the other side’s arrow

skins.title: The compost bin
skins.situation: Your building has a new compost bin. You and your neighbour Mohan each decide whether to sort your kitchen waste for it.

incentives.m3.s.both: Sorting your own waste gets you compost for your plants, and you gain more when Mohan sorts his too. The same holds for Mohan.

skins.timing: You both decide this week, separately.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know whether Mohan will sort.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your sorting and Mohan’s sorting

skins.title: Today’s class
skins.situation: Your tutor, Mrs Menon, decides whether to hold today’s class online or at her home. At the same time you decide whether to log in from home or travel to her house.

incentives.m3.s.one@B: You want to be wherever the class is held. Teaching online saves Mrs Menon setting up her front room for a class, and she would rather you log in.

skins.timing: You both decide this morning, separately.
skins.information: You know what Mrs Menon prefers. You don’t know where she will hold the class.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for Mrs Menon’s choice and yours

skins.title: Study for the exam
skins.situation: You and Tara are revising for the same exam this weekend. Each of you picks where to study: the library, the café, or a video call from home. You decide on Friday night, separately.

incentives.m3.s.stuck: You both want to study together, and the library and the café suit you equally well. A video call is your favourite if Tara joins one, and useless otherwise. Tara would rather go out than be on a call.

skins.timing: You both decide on Friday night, separately.
skins.information: You both know what the other wants. You don’t know where Tara will go.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your place and Tara’s place

skins.title: The shared tracker
skins.situation: You and Vivek must each keep this quarter’s project tracker in one place: the team spreadsheet, the team notebook, or a custom tool you built. Each of you sets up your part on Monday.

incentives.m3.s.stuck: Using the same place as Vivek saves you both work, and the spreadsheet and the notebook are equally good. Your tool is your favourite if Vivek uses it too. Vivek finds your tool slow and prefers either team option.

skins.timing: You both set up on Monday, separately.
skins.information: You both know what the other wants. You don’t know which Vivek will use.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your tracker and Vivek’s tracker

skins.title: Practice partners
skins.situation: You and Ishan practise tennis together on Saturdays. Each of you heads to court one, court two, or the gym for fitness drills, without checking with the other first.

incentives.m3.s.stuck: You both want to practise together, and the two courts are equally good. Gym drills are your favourite if Ishan comes, and wasted otherwise. Ishan would rather be on a court than in the gym.

skins.timing: You both set off on Saturday morning, separately.
skins.information: You both know what the other wants. You don’t know where Ishan will go.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your choice and Ishan’s choice

skins.title: Three rows, three columns
skins.situation: At the same moment, you pick a row, top, middle or bottom, and the other side picks a column, left, centre or right.

incentives.m3.s.stuck: Each of you wants a high number for yourself. Top-left and middle-centre are good for both. Bottom pays you well only with right, and the other side does worse with right than with left in every row.

skins.timing: You both pick at the same moment.
skins.information: Each side sees the whole table. You don’t know the other side’s column.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your row and the other side’s column

skins.title: The shared canal
skins.situation: You and Mr Gowda farm side by side. The canal stretch next to your field feeds his crops, and the stretch next to his feeds yours. This week each of you decides how long to spend clearing your stretch.

incentives.m3.s.pledge: Each half day you spend clearing costs you a half day of field work and brings Mr Gowda twice as much in water. His clearing does the same for you. The same holds for Mr Gowda.

skins.timing: You both decide on Monday, separately.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know how long Mr Gowda will clear.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your clearing and Mr Gowda’s clearing

skins.title: Client referrals
skins.situation: You and Priya are freelance designers. This month each of you decides how many client referrals to write for the other: two, one or none.

incentives.m3.s.pledge: Each referral you write costs you an afternoon of paid work and brings Priya twice that in new work. Her referrals do the same for you. The same holds for Priya.

skins.timing: You both decide at the start of the month, separately.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know how many Priya will write.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your referrals and Priya’s referrals

skins.title: Lending coaches
skins.situation: Your cricket club and Ms Khan’s club train juniors on the same ground. This season each club decides how many of its coaches to lend to the other club’s juniors: two, one or none.

incentives.m3.s.pledge: Each coach you lend costs your club a session and gives Ms Khan’s juniors twice that benefit. Her coaches do the same for your juniors. The same holds for Ms Khan.

skins.timing: Both clubs decide before the season, separately.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know how many coaches Ms Khan will lend.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your lending and Ms Khan’s lending

skins.title: Shop posters
skins.situation: You run a tea shop and Mrs Shah runs the bookshop at the other end of the lane. Each of you decides how many posters for the other’s shop to put up in your window: two, one or none.

incentives.m3.s.pledge: Each poster you put up takes window space you could use, and brings Mrs Shah twice that in customers. Her posters do the same for you. The same holds for Mrs Shah.

skins.timing: You both decide this week, separately.
skins.information: You both know what is at stake for each other. You don’t know how many posters Mrs Shah will put up.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your posters and Mrs Shah’s posters

skins.title: The wedding hall
skins.situation: You run a catering service. Mr Iyer, who owns a wedding hall, decides whether to book a day event or a night event. At the same time you decide whether to bring your spare generator.

incentives.m3.s.weakb@B: In daylight the generator stays off, and Mr Iyer pays for it either way. At night, power cuts are common, and a generator saves your service. Mr Iyer prefers a night event only if a generator is there.

skins.timing: You both decide this week, separately.
skins.information: You know how Mr Iyer plans. You don’t know which event he will book.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for Mr Iyer’s booking and your choice

skins.title: The evening walk
skins.situation: Your friend Anand picks the route for this evening’s walk: the valley path, which ends before dark, or the ridge path, which ends after dark. You pack your bag at the same time.

incentives.m3.s.weakb@B: On the valley path a torch makes no difference to you. On the ridge path, a torch is what gets you down safely. Anand enjoys the ridge only if someone has a torch; otherwise he prefers the valley.

skins.timing: You both decide at home, separately.
skins.information: You know what Anand likes. You don’t know which path he will pick.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for Anand’s route and your packing

skins.title: The client pitch
skins.situation: Your colleague Neel decides whether tomorrow’s pitch happens in your office or at the client’s. You decide whether to carry the team projector with you.

incentives.m3.s.weakb@B: In your office a projector is already set up, so carrying one changes nothing. At the client’s, your own projector is what makes the pitch work. Neel prefers the client’s office only if you bring it.

skins.timing: You both decide this evening, separately.
skins.information: You know how Neel plans. You don’t know where he will hold the pitch.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for Neel’s venue and your choice

skins.title: Arrow and dial
skins.situation: At the same moment, the other side points an arrow up or down, and you turn a dial left or right.

incentives.m3.s.weakb@B: With up, left and right give you the same. With down, left gives you more than right. The other side does better with down when you turn left, and with up when you turn right.

skins.timing: You both choose at the same moment.
skins.information: Each side sees the whole table. You don’t know where the arrow will point.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for the arrow and your dial

skins.title: The team outing
skins.situation: Rina is planning Friday for your team: lunch in the office, or an outing to the lake. At the same time you decide whether to book the society’s van, which members may book at no charge.

incentives.m3.s.weakb@B: If lunch is in the office, the van just stays parked. For an outing, the van is the only way the whole team gets there. Rina prefers the outing only if the van is booked.

skins.timing: You both decide on Wednesday, separately.
skins.information: You know how Rina plans. You don’t know which she will choose.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for Rina’s plan and your booking

skins.title: Two food trucks
skins.situation: You and Rahul run food trucks and share one generator, so you must park together to open. Each of you picks a spot for Saturday: the stadium, the college, or the night market.

incentives.m3.s.stuck: Parking together lets you both open, and the stadium and the college are equally good. The night market is your best spot if Rahul comes too. Rahul has no permit there and does worse there than at the stadium.

skins.timing: You both decide on Thursday, separately.
skins.information: You both know what the other wants. You don’t know where Rahul will park.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your spot and Rahul’s spot

items.prompt: Is one of your choices better for you whatever {them} does? Pick the best reason.

verdict.yes: So {dom:you} gives you more whatever {them} does.
verdict.no: So neither choice gives you more in both cases.

optionSets.text: Yes, {act:a1}: if {them} picks {act:b1} it gives you {pay:you:a1:b1}, not {pay:you:a2:b1}; if {act:b2}, {pay:you:a1:b2}, not {pay:you:a2:b2}.
No: which of your choices is better depends on whether {them} picks {act:b1} or {act:b2} this time.
Yes, {act:a1}: if {them} picks {act:b1} it gives you {pay:you:a1:b1}, not {pay:you:a2:b1}, and that settles it.
{Act:a1}, because it gives you more whether {them} picks {act:b1} ({pay:you:a1:b1} to {pay:you:a2:b1}) or {act:b2} ({pay:you:a1:b2} to {pay:you:a2:b2}).
{Act:a1}, because it gave you a good outcome the last time this came up, so it will again.
Neither, because your better choice changes with what {them} picks, {act:b1} or {act:b2}.

No: which of your choices is better depends on what {them} does.
